A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures and appendices A–E are readable and can be matched despite pagination changes.

before.justification: Section 7 reports original Message Flooding experiments and architectural ablations. Appendix C includes random-graph evaluations, algorithm-instruction verification and collision experiments.

after.justification: Section 7 and Appendix C retain the original empirical results, including ensemble-accuracy curves and perfect NTK-based instruction verification on the tested graphs.

M1.justification: The ensemble GNN, block encoding, Heaviside thresholding, masking and algorithm instructions are unchanged. Expanded template descriptions explain constructions already documented in Appendix D.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Message Flooding on trees, random graphs, complete graphs and stars, and verify Flooding, BFS, DFS and Bellman-Ford instructions in Appendix C.1. No datasets, tasks or test scenarios are added.

E2.justification: The same encoding/Heaviside variants and direct-write versus cascade-chain strategies are compared. Newly cited research is discussed without being introduced as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Sections 7 and C retain the same graph generation, parameter sweeps, accuracy criteria and NTK substitutions. Sample sizes remain 100 graphs per algorithm in C.1 and 2,000 graphs per test set in C.2.

E4.justification: The encoding and Heaviside ablations in Section 7.3, instruction checks in C.1 and collision analysis in C.3 retain the same questions, procedures and evidence.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests relative to the other.

E6.justification: Figures 3–7 and the Appendix C findings are unchanged, including perfect instruction verification and collision-related failure at nine or more nodes for direct writes. No result entries are added or corrected.

T1.justification: Theorems 5.1 and 6.1–6.4 add explicit infinite-width conditions omitted from their earlier statements. This aligns the statements with v1's existing NTK assumptions; the bounds and appendix proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction now explicitly qualifies its exact-learnability claim as applying in the infinite-width regime. The abstract and the contributions concerning LOCAL, Message Flooding, BFS, DFS and Bellman-Ford are retained.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds an explicit qualification that GNN iteration counts should not be directly compared with LOCAL rounds, which exclude local computation costs. Previously, this passage explained the difference from centralized algorithm complexity. Section 8's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The detailed encodings, training-data construction, algorithm instructions and code-access information are retained. Added cross-references and explanations point to technical material already present in v1.

R1.justification: Adds discussion and citations for György, Garnier, Gilmer and Hashemi, and revises the characterization of Nerem's optimization guarantees. The central positioning relative to Back de Luca and Loukas remains. Malach's reference changes publication metadata for the same work.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify template/block terminology, direct algorithm constructions and ensemble-complexity scaling. Cross-references, heading capitalization and acknowledgments are updated, while the section organization and most prose remain stable.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves from page 2 to a dedicated page 3, and Model 2 and several figures shift relative to surrounding text. All nine figure graphics and their captions are retained; no figures or tables are added or redesigned.

improvement.justification: Making the infinite-width condition explicit in the introduction and main theorem statements reduces the risk of interpreting the guarantees as finite-width results. The LOCAL-round comparison and expanded research context also improve precision. These are limited gains because the underlying assumptions were already disclosed and the proofs and empirical evidence are unchanged.
